classification.difficultyReason: Recognise reflection symmetry about the y-axis and rotational symmetry about the origin in six supplied graphs.

inlines.text: Classify the following functions by their graph as either even, odd or neither.

spec.sourceRegion: Essential problems, questions 19–24, first row left: printed question 19.
spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with its vertex at the unlabelled origin and outward arrowheads at both upper ends. Black coordinate axes labelled x and y; no ticks, numerical labels or grid.
spec.mathematics: The two branches are reflections in the y-axis. The quadratic path uses normalised drawing coordinates only; no equation or numerical scale is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph is permanent question content. Its classification appears only in the answers.

answer.worked: The graph has reflection symmetry about the $y$-axis, so the function is even.

spec.sourceRegion: Essential problems, questions 19–24, first row right: printed question 20.
spec.description: Increasing cubic-shaped curve through the unlabelled origin with a horizontal tangent there. Arrowheads extend into quadrants III and I. Black coordinate axes labelled x and y; no ticks, numerical labels or grid.
spec.mathematics: Opposite branches correspond under a half-turn about the origin. The cubic path is an unscaled graphical reconstruction, not an additional supplied equation.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph is permanent question content. Its classification appears only in the answers.

answer.worked: The graph has $180^\circ$ rotational symmetry about the origin, so the function is odd.

spec.sourceRegion: Essential problems, questions 19–24, second row left: printed question 21.
spec.description: Increasing exponential-shaped curve entirely above the x-axis, crossing the y-axis above the origin. Its left tail approaches the x-axis and its right branch rises steeply; both ends have arrowheads. Black axes labelled x and y; no ticks, numerical labels or grid.
spec.mathematics: The supplied shape has neither y-axis reflection symmetry nor origin rotational symmetry. Normalised drawing coordinates preserve the qualitative shape without adding an equation or numerical intercept.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph is permanent question content. Its classification appears only in the answers.

answer.worked: The graph has neither reflection symmetry about the $y$-axis nor $180^\circ$ rotational symmetry about the origin. The function is neither even nor odd.

spec.sourceRegion: Essential problems, questions 19–24, second row right: printed question 22.
spec.description: Upper semicircle centred at the unlabelled origin, with symmetric endpoints on the x-axis and its highest point on the positive y-axis. No curve arrowheads or endpoint markers. Black axes labelled x and y; no numerical scale or grid.
spec.mathematics: Equal x and y drawing units retain a semicircle and reflection symmetry about the y-axis. The drawing radius is unlabelled and is not a source numerical given.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph is permanent question content. Its classification appears only in the answers.

answer.worked: The semicircle has reflection symmetry about the $y$-axis, so the function is even.

spec.sourceRegion: Essential problems, questions 19–24, third row left: printed question 23.
spec.description: Finite decreasing S-shaped curve with two closed endpoints. The left endpoint is in quadrant II; the right endpoint lies on the positive x-axis. The curve crosses the y-axis above the origin. Black axes labelled x and y; no curve arrows, numerical coordinates, ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: The curve is a function and has neither of the required symmetries. Its finite endpoints and positive y-intercept are retained. Bézier coordinates are unscaled drawing controls, not added mathematical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied curve and both closed endpoint markers are permanent question content. Its classification appears only in the answers.

answer.worked: The graph has neither reflection symmetry about the $y$-axis nor $180^\circ$ rotational symmetry about the origin. The function is neither even nor odd.

spec.sourceRegion: Essential problems, questions 19–24, third row right: printed question 24.
spec.description: Smooth positive mound symmetric about the y-axis, with a maximum on that axis and outward arrowheads on both low tails. Black coordinate axes labelled x and y; no numerical labels, ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: The two halves are exact reflections in the y-axis. Symmetric Bézier controls preserve the unscaled source silhouette without asserting an equation or numerical maximum.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph is permanent question content. Its classification appears only in the answers.

answer.worked: The graph has reflection symmetry about the $y$-axis, so the function is even.
